Toulouse vs Rennes - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.
  • Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 01:56.

Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.

Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.

For the second time domestically this season, Toulouse failed to emerge victorious last week when scoring first.

Those four points dropped represent the difference between their current position and a spot in Europe next season.

On the other hand, they have avoided defeat in seven of their last eight league games, including the last three at Stadium de Toulouse.

In their last three Ligue 1 home contests, this team have netted a combined six goals, six more than in their opening two games played in Toulouse.

Discipline has been an glitch for Jens Berthel Askou’s men in the top flight this season, as they average the second-most fouls per match in the competition (15.7).

Toulouse can extend their Ligue 1 home unbeaten run versus Rennes on Sunday to five matches, last beating them in Toulouse in 2025 (2-1).

A campaign that began with so much promise has deteriorated for Stade Rennais, who have struggled to find consistency this month.

Franck Haise’s men are on a five-match winless run across all competitions, having begun 2026-27 unbeaten in their first five competitive fixtures.

A 3-1 loss at NEC in Europa League action on Thursday has them narrowly above the knockout stage line in that competition.

In November, they have netted a goal or fewer in each of their competitive games, while conceding a combined six times in their last three competitive outings.

Away from home, Rennes have really been exposed defensively in the league, conceding a combined 14 goals in their last four domestic matches as the visitors.

Les Rouge et Noirs are second in the league regarding expected goals, though they have conceded more penalties than anyone in the competition so far (five).

Rennes form (all competitions):.

Toulouse may be without Mark McKenzie, who suffered a hamstring strain in their last match, while Aron Donnum is eligible to return from his suspension.

Jacen Russell-Rowe netted for them in the opening half at Lens, his third of the Ligue 1 campaign, tied with Thomas Jorgensen for second on the team.

A minor knock has Valentin Rongier questionable in this outing for Rennes, while Adrien Thomasson will miss the match with a red-card suspension.

Boulaye Dia scored in their draw at arch-rivals Lorient last Sunday, putting him up to six in the league this season, one fewer than last season’s leading goalscorer in Ligue 1, Esteban Lepaul.

Toulouse possible starting lineup:.

Restes; Diallo, Koumbassa, Nicolaisen, Tape; Jorgensen, Casseres, Sigur, Russell-Rowe; Vignolo, Tengstedt.

Rennes possible starting lineup:.

Samba; Reynolds, Cresswell, Oliveira, Rouault; Cisse; Al-Taamari, Blas, Camara; Dia, Lepaul.

As much as they have struggled of late, we believe Rennes' firepower will be sharper this weekend and punish a Toulouse backline that is far from reassuring defensively.

Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.
  • More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.
  • In a recent development, in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.

More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.

In a recent development, in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost. And since 1990, nearly 490 million hectares of forest have been wiped out.

According to recent reports, more recently, the trend has shifted in the opposite direction. Deforestation in the Amazon region of Brazil decreased by 41% from August 2025 through 2026 to reach its lowest rate since records began.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

To ensure lasting protection, the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was debuted in 2025 at the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

Because rainforests are so important for the world, the idea behind the fund was to give money to the countries where they are located to help them preserve and protect these ecosystems.

So far, these countries have made more profit through deforestation — for example, by mining natural resources on rainforest land or farming the area.

According to recent reports, starting in 2027, the TFFF is expected to generate the funds needed for rainforest conservation, in part via contributions from various countries. By the end of this year, a total of $10 billion (€8.9 billion) in government capital is due to flow into the fund, mainly in the form of low-interest loans.

In addition, the TFFF is expected to issue bonds to private investors, such as banks and investment firms, to raise additional funds — initially totaling about $40 billion.

Going forward, the strategy is for governments to contribute a total of $25 billion to the pot, and for private donors to contribute $100 billion. The fund will then invest this money in international financial markets with the aim of generating profits.

Private investors who purchase TFFF bonds can expect to earn about 5% interest per bond per year, noted Felix Finkbeiner, the founder of the German environmental organization Plant-for-the-Planet, where he is responsible for forest conservation and advocacy.

"Private investors' capital is very well protected," Finkbeiner stated, adding that any losses the TFFF might incur on the capital markets — for example, if the price of its bonds should fall — would be offset by government funds.

About 2.7% of the TFFF's profits would be set aside for countries with tropical forests.

According to recent reports, countries would receive $4 per year for every hectare of forest that they preserve instead of chopping down. At least 20% of these funds must be allocated to Indigenous peoples and local communities.

According to calculations by the TFFF Watch website, an independent platform rolled out by Plant-for-the-Planet to track investments, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, would receive about $333 million for its 2024 forest stock under this system.

It has been revealed that finkbeiner noted the subsidies would be paid only for intact ecosystems and not for timber plantations, with forest areas and their condition mapped and assessed using satellite imagery. Though it can sometimes be difficult to identify plantations accurately on satellite photos, he said, the technology has improved significantly over the last decade.

That means any NGO or external party with access to the satellite data can check the condition of the region, providing further oversight. If forest areas are cleared or damaged, money is deducted from the total.

Another safeguard: If countries don't use the TFFF funds for rainforest conservation, their payments could be frozen for the next few years.

The TFFF is supposed to invest, whenever possible, in government bonds issued by emerging and developing countries. Above all, the idea is not to invest in projects that harm the climate — such as those linked to oil, gas, or coal investments.

The TFFF concept has received plenty of support from environmental organizations, in part because it gives countries in the Global South significantly more sovereignty than traditional forms of development financing.

"For example, if the government of Ghana wants to protect its rainforest today, it usually asks the World Bank for financial assistance — and then the World Bank in [Washington] DC decides whether Ghana is allowed to do so," Finkbeiner stated.

The TFFF fund is also designed to be immune to donor countries' backing out in the event of a change in government, for example. Once a contribution is made, the money remains in the fund for 40 years before being paid back.

Sources indicate that continuing protection is also an incentive for countries receiving money from the fund. "When a new government comes into power that wants to cut back a little on climate protection, they will realize: We'll get more money if we protect the rainforest," stated Finkbeiner.

Industry observers note that for the rainforest fund to actually get off the ground, a total of $10 billion in seed capital must be raised by the end of 2026. So far, the confirmed pledges from countries, NGOs and foundations total only $7.9 billion.

Eight countries have expressed a willingness to contribute so far, including Brazil, Indonesia, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Norway, with a pledge of $3 billion, is the largest would-be donor. However, the government in Oslo is willing to honor its commitment only if the agreed-upon total amount is in place by the end of the year.

"This deadline isn't set in stone, but otherwise the Norwegian government will have real trouble getting it through parliament," Finkbeiner remarked.

It has been revealed that germany's commitment must also still be approved by the parliament. The German government has pledged about €1 billion to the TFFF starting in 2027, to be paid out over 10 years.

Other countries are also considering investing in the TFFF, including Canada, China, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates.

Sources indicate that philanthropic organizations have pledged $88 million to the fund so far, including $73 million announced this week during the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Finkbeiner remains upbeat.

It has been revealed that "Promises like that always come at the last minute," he said. "I'm very optimistic that we'll secure more commitments at the COP — and in the course of December — and that we'll then reach that $10 billion.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Brazilian's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, it doesn't feel like the Reds are going to offer him a latest deal.
  • Indeed, rumours about both ends of the deal have been emerging and, even though the former Roma man has been an crucial asset for Liverpool this term, his age coupled with the sheer number of goalkeepers the Reds have on their books make a deal difficult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alisson is one of Liverpool's biggest-named players to be linked with an exit this summer.

The Brazilian's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, it doesn't feel like the Reds are going to offer him a latest deal.

Indeed, rumours about both ends of the deal have been emerging and, even though the former Roma man has been an crucial asset for Liverpool this term, his age coupled with the sheer number of goalkeepers the Reds have on their books make a deal difficult.

Obviously, Alisson's time at the club has been well regarded. He's won two Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy.

But, since he's now in the twilight stages of his career, Liverpool need to approach this deal with caution and weigh up their options before making a final decision.

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool could make a move.

Having a decent goalkeeper is one of the most important things for any football team.

Even if you have one of the best teams in the world in terms of outfielders, if your goalkeeper is poor, they're more than likely going to let you down.

This was the case when Giorgi Mamardashvili played last season with fans demanding that a latest 'keeper was signed.

Initially, the Georgian was expected to take over from the Brazilian but, thanks to how poorly he performed, that didn't end up being the case.

Mamardashvili's poor form led to fans wondering who their next goalkeeper could be with a fresh revision from L'Equipe now making that more than clear.

"Lucas Chevalier is ready to leave Paris Saint-Germain this winter. But there are many conditions for a departure. PSG will notably have to find a replacement before considering letting him go," they wrote.

Lucas Chevalier would be an out of the box signing for Liverpool.

When Chevalier was brought to PSG by Luis Enrique, fans, pundits and journalists all thought that the Frenchman was destined to become their first choice.

Obviously he had some massive shoes to fill after Gianluigi Donnarumma exited for Manchester City but, for Enrique's style of play, the Frenchman was the better option.

But, for one reason or another, the 25-year-old didn't hit the right notes and has been downgraded to their back-up by Matvey Safonov.

Neither of them are considered among the world's best but, Chevalier is almost certainly a better option for Liverpool than Mamardashvili would be.

Others such as Bart Verbruggen and Diogo Costa have also been linked with Liverpool but, since Chevalier actually wants to exit, a deal for him might be easier for Liverpool to agree on with PSG.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for any of Liverpool's first team squad but, if Chevalier is a player welcomed through the Anfield doors, the Reds will be in a decent place, even if he is replacing Alisson.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan produced a stunning come-from-behind victory against Olympiacos, scoring four times unanswered to win 4-2.

Recent findings suggest that it looked like being another miserable European night for Milan, as they fell two goals behind inside 50 minutes. The first was given as a Mike Maignan own-goal after Lorenzo Pirola’s header from a corner hit the crossbar then the goalkeeper, then Jota Silva doubled the advantage.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Out of nowhere, Milan mounted a comeback inside 15 second-half minutes. Omari Hutchinson inspired it, scoring a wonderful solo goal to halve the deficit, then setting up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser, and also providing the assist for Christian Pulisic’s goal off the bench.

Diego Moreira finished a counter-attack right at the end of the game to make it 4-2 and seal the result, one that was very much needed for Milan given their start in the competition. The play-off hopes have been dealt a big boost, while the top eight could still be a possibility too.

Amorim made four changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Frosinone on Sunday. Two were enforced due to injuries, with Ardon Jashari replacing Luka Modric and Pervis Estupinan taking Davide Bartesaghi’s spot. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchinson came into the attack.

The first shot of the game took less than two minutes to come and it provided an example of the intense pressing that the home side have become known for, though Freuler’s effort from distance was a speculative one that sailed comfortably over.

Milan began to string some nice moves together, and they had a couple of attempts of their own from just beyond the edge of the box miss the target. The first came from Cisse, who cut inside and curled one well over and wide, then Jashari concluded a promising attack with a wild shot.

Recent findings suggest that there were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

The first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

According to recent reports, olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

The trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Milan were inches away from getting themselves level promptly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. A ball over the top found Cisse’s run in behind and Ortega came darting off his line but the ball squirmed through. The Italian somehow got a shot off from the floor that was rolling into the net but for Lirola’s last-ditch sliding clearance for a corner.

There was a flash point towards the end of the half which saw De Winter and Jota Silva both go into the box. A long ball over the top was eventually followed by play being blown dead for offside, yet the pair had a stand-up wrestling match for about 20 yards, until they both even ended up off the field.

In the first of two minutes added on at the end of the half, Pirola had a chance to actually get his name on the scoresheet after the opener was labelled an own-goal. Some dire defending down the right ended with a cut-back that the former Inter youth academy man fired over from inside the box.

In a recent development, amorim chose to make two changes at the break, as the American duo Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah came on. Ramos and Estupinan were the ones to make way, with Cisse going up front and Moreira switching over to left wing-back.

Within four minutes of the restart, Olympiacos doubled their lead after yet more calamitous defending. De Winter continued his trend of failing to strong together multiple games without errors as he played a stray pass out from the back, allowing Freuler to play though Jota Silva, who fired past Maignan first time.

De Winter then gave away a sloppy foul when it looked like he had brought a ball under his control and Amorim had seen enough, bringing Fikayo Tomori on for the Belgian.

Industry observers note that just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. Having seized possession inside his own half, the Englishman went on a brilliant solo run down the right where he was nearly clipped down twice, before jinking inside onto his preferred left foot and finding the bottom corner with a precise low shot.

In a recent development, milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. A sustained period of possession inside the Olympiacos half saw the ball worked nicely down the right side for Hutchinson to cross perfectly onto the head of Cisse at the far post, who headed in from a few yards out for his 10th of the campaign.

In a recent development, as if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. The substitute struck his volley perfectly, nestling it inside the post.

Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

According to recent reports, with just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays showed it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2551 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of \({\mathcal{O}}(1)\) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

Auxerre vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00.
  • Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.
  • After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00.

Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.

After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.

After a rough start to the 2026-27 campaign, it appears as though Auxerre are doing just enough to get by domestically.

Will Still’s men lost their first three matches of this top-flight season, but have since collected points in six of their last eight league fixtures.

That has them just a point above Strasbourg who are in the relegation playoff spot heading into matchday 12 with Auxerre just three points above Angers, who are in the last automatic relegation position.

So far this season AJA have yet to lose a Ligue 1 fixture when netting the opening goal, with their draw versus Monaco last week being the first time they dropped points in that position.

They lead the league regarding fouls per match (16.1) while allowing the joint-most goals in this competition after 11 matchdays (25).

AJA have points in three of their last four Ligue 1 fixtures at home, with their last win at Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps occuring in September against Brest (2-1).

Marseille will hope their late collapse against Le Mans serves as a temporary speed bump and a wake-up call going forward.

Bruno Genesio’s side bounced back well in midweek, defeating Levski Sofia 1-0 in Europa League action, putting them into the knockout places in that competition.

Clean sheets like the one they collected on Thursday have been rare for OM in Ligue 1, as they have conceded a 2.40 xG average following their defeat to Le Mans in the top flight.

Fortunately, they are balancing that out with plenty of goals, averaging the second-most goals per game in Ligue 1 (2.2) heading into matchday 12.

After 11 matchdays, only three points currently separate them from the top three and a place in next season’s Champions League.

Les Olympiens will seek a third successive triumph versus Auxerre in this competition, having won both Ligue 1 meetings against them last season 1-0.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Both Bryan Okoh and Assane Diousse will miss this match for Auxerre as they recover from cruciate ligament tears, while Sekou Fofana has a groin strain and Danny Loader is questionable with an ankle injury.

Romain Faivre scored their only goal on matchday 11, the second of the campaign for the man currently on loan from Bournemouth.

At Marseille, Derek Cornelius is still recovering from a hip problem, Emerson Palmieri is questionable with a knee injury and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is questionable because of an illness.

Amine Gouiri scored the winner in their Europa League victory on Thursday, becoming the first OM player to net in five successive competitive fixtures since Florian Thauvin in 2018, while he and Igor Paixao scored in their defeat to Le Mans.

Auxerre possible starting lineup:.

Nardi; Diomande, Tuanzebe, Siwe; Senaya, Ahamada, Danois, Oppegard; Faivre, Lascary; Archer.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Kamissoko, Nnadi; Gomes, Maupay, Paixao; Gouiri.

These are two of the most inconsistent defensive units in the league, and in a match which could be wide open for that reason, we believe the quality of the visitors, who have fared well in those kinds of matches this season, will enable them to prevail.

#153181. Opinion: Sensational player has officially announced himself as Liverpool's newest star

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (460 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Opinion: Sensational player has officially announced himself as Liverpool's newest star

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One player has officially declared himself as a key player with a fantastic performance.
  • According to recent reports, liverpool went into this season with a very imbalanced squad.
  • Of course, that's largely the job of a head coach but it's rare that so much experimentation was necessary from a UEFA Champions League side that won the Premier League two seasons ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have a new star. One player has officially declared himself as a key player with a fantastic performance.

According to recent reports, liverpool went into this season with a very imbalanced squad. It was one that required a lot from newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola, essentially asking him to improve and experiment with players to get the most out of it.

Of course, that's largely the job of a head coach but it's rare that so much experimentation was necessary from a UEFA Champions League side that won the Premier League two seasons ago. But that's what Liverpool offered Iraola after two transfer windows that tore up large portions of the team.

No defensive midfielders, no recognised right-back, four left-wingers, no right-wingers, and one fit centre-forward. Hardly a 'win now' group of players. Iraola, though, has worked some real magic.

According to recent reports, and that includes solving the defensive midfielder problem. At least for now.

Sources indicate that the midfielder problem was a surprise one. We fully expected Liverpool to invest in the middle of the pitch over the summer but they simply ignored the issue. Even more bizarre was a decision to sell Curtis Jones without any sort of replacement.

It left Iraola short but it's a problem he appears to have fixed. Trey Nyoni has stepped up incredibly well, moving from a mere youth player who hoped for minutes to a genuine starting threat in the span of just a few months.

Wednesday night, though, felt like an announcement of sorts. Nyoni started away from home in the UEFA Champions League and thrived, holding down the midfield against a rampant Club Brugge.

Liverpool’s clean sheet made them the first team to hold out against Brugge for a very, very long time. The first team to beat Brugge in months, too.

Nyoni played his part. He wasn’t necessarily a defensive force by the way he won tackles here, it was more about his efforts on the ball to keep Liverpool ticking over.

92 per cent pass completion away from home in the Champions League is fantastic. It’s even more fantastic that he did it while completing 11 line-breaking passes - this wasn’t a case of Nyoni simply picking the simple ball every time.

Industry observers note that that 11 was the third-highest figure in the match and second-highest for Liverpool (Jeremy Jacquet had 13). It’s exactly the kind of midfield play that the Reds have been crying out for and doing it at a difficult ground in the premiere competition is just outstanding from a 19-year-old.

Nyoni is special and this felt like an announcement. Confirmation that he is a proper star player and one Liverpool can count on in major fixtures.

Chelsea transfer news: Blues 'closely monitor' Boca Juniors centre-back ahead of 2027

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (394 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11.
  • Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.
  • The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11.

Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.

The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.

After making his senior bow in August, the former captain of Boca’s reserve side swiftly established himself in the first team and helped the club win the Copa Sudamericana in Barranquilla last week.

Herrera impressed in the 2-0 final triumph over Atletico Mineiro, completing 56 of 58 passes and recording nine clearances as Boca kept a clean sheet.

Argentine publications El Crack Deportivo and Clarin via Sport Witness report that Chelsea scouts are closely assessing Herrera's physical and technical progress as part of the club’s continuing recruitment drive in South America.

The 1.80m right-footer has earned plaudits for his speed, aerial strength and composure when playing through the opposition’s press from the back.

Herrera highlighted his eye for a decisive moment on October 25 by scoring his first senior goal with a late winner against Independiente that secured Boca's place at the top of the annual league standings.

The youngster's growing standing has attracted praise from some of Argentina’s most respected figures: Boca's record appearance-maker Roberto Mouzo has likened him to 1978 World Cup winner Alberto Tarantini, while Oscar Ruggeri has called on national team manager Lionel Scaloni to give him senior minutes straight away.

Chelsea are not the only club following the youngster. Barcelona are reportedly seeking scouting reports ahead of January, while Benfica, Borussia Dortmund and Porto have also been linked with him.

Despite increasing interest from England and elsewhere in Europe, a move to prise Herrera away from La Bombonera in 2027 is unlikely to be straightforward.

Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme is determined to keep the heart of his trophy-winning squad together as the club prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

Head coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena has also told the board he wants the defender to stay, praising his strength in one-on-one duels and his willingness to learn from more experienced team-mates.

Boca have yet to receive a formal offer or begin transfer talks, putting the club in a strong position to resist early approaches while Herrera continues to develop in Buenos Aires.

Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.
  • Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.
  • This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SIGNIFICANT) campaign called "The King's Return.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (SIGNIFICANT) campaign called "The King's Return.".

In a recent development, MASSIVE, a Christian group for footballers, has said it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

"Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he mentioned.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

Industry observers note that "I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then remarked that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

According to recent reports, in Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp mentioned, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

Klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

"We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

#153177. Mauricio Pochettino is creating a siege mentality straight out of Sir Alex Ferguson's playbook - the refereeing horror show in Lisbon is just more ammunition, writes NATHAN SALT

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1318 w)

Mauricio Pochettino is creating a siege mentality straight out of Sir Alex Ferguson's playbook - the refereeing horror show in Lisbon is just more ammunition, writes NATHAN SALT

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:10 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 02:50 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino's job at Manchester United is hard enough without match officials getting in his way.
  • He's got to raise the physical floor of this team, embed a high-press playing style that's at odds with the laxer approach of predecessor Michael Carrick, rid this group of individual mistakes that continue to plague the dressing room, battle against mounting injuries and suspensions, work with a modest transfer budget, navigate the press, create an identity that appears to have been lost and do it all playing every three to four days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:10 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 02:50 EST, 26 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino's job at Manchester United is hard enough without match officials getting in his way.

He's got to raise the physical floor of this team, embed a high-press playing style that's at odds with the laxer approach of predecessor Michael Carrick, rid this group of individual mistakes that continue to plague the dressing room, battle against mounting injuries and suspensions, work with a modest transfer budget, navigate the press, create an identity that appears to have been lost and do it all playing every three to four days.

It has been revealed that but where Carrick looked eager to put out fires – part of his original appeal to bosses was his ability to steer clear of the headlines his predecessor, Ruben Amorim, brought with such frequency - Pochettino is keen to pour petrol on them and it's lit a fire that everyone inside the building is embracing. It's straight out of Sir Alex Ferguson's playbook.

Pochettino grew up idolising the greatness of Ferguson and when they shared a private lunch together in 2016, it would become a key moment in Pochettino's own managerial journey to here, now the man leading Manchester United.

In Ferguson's mind, and this was shared with Pochettino that day over lunch, he must spin two plates simultaneously to thrive at a club the size of United.

In a recent development, the very best coaches can play a game on the pitch and one in the press. To Ferguson, winning off the pitch was as crucial as winning on it.

Mauricio Pochettino has shown in the space of a week how he can channel Sir Alex Ferguson.

A lot of what Pochettino has done thus far feels like it's straight out of idol Ferguson's playbook.

'Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him,' Pochettino recently said. It indicates.

So much of what Pochettino has done so far has got Ferguson's fingerprints all over it. They were all over the pre-match interview ahead of the Sporting clash when he was asked about his start to life in Manchester.

'You've had a game as Manchester United manager now…' the interviewer began.

To which Pochettino replied: 'No. I've had EIGHT minutes,' referencing the small section against Liverpool prior to Leny Yoro's unjust sending off.

Those same fingerprints were also over the club's fiercely front-footed response to ProRef following the decision for Yoro's red to be overturned. Howard Webb doubled down on the original decision, a call Pochettino and the club believed was 'totally wrong'. United are now taking up their irritation with the Premier League. Top flight referees are understood to be livid.

And then there's Lisbon, a night of total chaos, most inflicted by referee Szymon Marciniak who chalked off a legitimate goal for Amad due to a non-foul by Youri Tielemans, which he was booked for. Marciniak would later send Tielemans off having already chalked off a match-winning goal for United due to an alleged infringement by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper. All of this came after he was conned into giving a penalty against Lisandro Martinez. Pochettino bounced around his technical area like Tigger, apoplectic at the unjustness of it all.

He will wait on another apology that will do nothing other than play into the siege mentality he is trying to create.

Industry observers note that pochettino has only been in the building a week and already he is embracing the spirit of Ferguson. Where that would lead Ferguson's United to major finals and titles, now it could be the key to Pochettino salvaging a season that has threatened to get majorly out of hand.

Pochettino's fury at decisions made against his team are protecting this fragile dressing room.

Pochettino has proven to have a firm grip on the media side so far, dictating the narratives.

He's not short of ammunition either.

His first training session, which exposed his desire to play Bryan Mbeumo out wide, use a back-three at times in possession, and have Joshua Zirkzee as a focal point, was recorded on a rogue drone that soon published its findings on YouTube. More than 100,000 views later it disappeared.

In a recent development, then the trip to Anfield where Yoro was shown a straight red card – wrongly – for a last-man foul on Alexander Isak. An independent panel retrospectively overturned the decision 5-0, even if ProRef chief Howard Webb doubled down to back the original call.

Pochettino, armed with research, even pointed out how the opening goal from Dominik Szoboszlai should not have stood due to illegal interference with the defensive wall by Liverpool's Bradley Barcola.

According to recent reports, many had not even got that on the rap sheet. Pochettino cleverly planted another seed of injustice.

'Maybe the rules changed while I was in America?' Pochettino remarked sarcastically.

It has been revealed that 'Why didn't they check it? It should have been disallowed. I'm here to defend my players and my club.'.

And so a furious United headed for Lisbon and were subjected to abysmal officiating that played into Pochettino's hands in terms of masking the individual errors that were as costly as the officials.

Bruno Fernandes scored a brace in Portugal on a night where Pochettino's ideas were obvious.

His demonstrative nature on touchline contrasts to Michael Carrick - and players responded.

'It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game,' Pochettino noted. 'We were punished a lot in key actions.'.

Ferguson would defend players publicly and point fingers at officials and Pochettino has so far proven to be no different.

Industry observers note that on a night where goalkeeper Senne Lammens made two particularly costly errors, a sign of his struggles this season, Pochettino embraced him on the pitch and in the media. If anything, the defence in front of the Belgian had to shoulder the manager's blame.

Industry observers note that noussair Mazraoui, too, was culpable of really poor positioning for Sporting's opening goal, just like Matthijs de Ligt was at Anfield. In back-to-back matches, Pochettino has finished with 10 men. Each and every player got nothing but universal backing publicly.

According to recent reports, players are looking to the touchline and seeing a head coach they can respond to. Players unquestionably let down Carrick and have done their level best to drag Pochettino down in moments, too, but he's demonstrative, emotional and a totemic figure for them to rally behind.

In a recent development, there were signs in Lisbon of the identity that Pochettino is imprinting, signs of the high-press style, signs of a structure that has been so badly lacking, signs of a initiative, a method to lifting them off the canvas and have them back swinging punches domestically and in Europe. There were signs, too, that Pochettino and his staff have lots of work to do to flush this dressing room of the mistake culture that has crept in.

By pointing fingers at the officials, Pochettino is shielding this fragile dressing room from even more scrutiny than it has already faced. Just like his managerial idol, he's proving a master of creating the siege mentality that could be the key to getting United out of the mess he's inherited them in.

'He persuaded us Manchester United are the team everyone loves to hate,' Ryan Giggs famously said of Ferguson in 2022.

Industry observers note that 'He makes us feel everyone wants us to come second and it is us against the world. He lays down the challenge for you to take up.'.

Now it's Pochettino who is creating his own version. Watching his protege from the stands, no doubt Ferguson is beaming with pride.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

In a recent development, obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

Industry observers note that holland was the one who sparked the issue originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

He was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

Elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

According to recent reports, maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Industry observers note that finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he said:.

“A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager demonstrates me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”.

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

Sources indicate that right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

#153174. Opinion: Richard Hughes' bargain deal has saved Liverpool's season

Opinion: Richard Hughes' bargain deal has saved Liverpool's season

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.
  • They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.
  • Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is currently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on upcoming players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes.

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has promptly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks.

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he rapidly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:29, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:31.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly facing a fee of at least €80m (£67m) if they are to tempt teenage defender Joane Gadou away from Borussia Dortmund.

The 19-year-old French centre-back has made a swift breakthrough in Germany after joining from Red Bull Salzburg for €20m (£16.8m) last summer.

Dortmund believe they have found another exceptional prospect with the potential to make his mark on the international stage, and his estimated market value has reportedly already risen by 40% to €28m (£23.5m) according to Sport Witness.

The former Paris Saint-Germain academy player, recently linked with Liverpool, is under contract for the long term and has no release clause, leaving the Bundesliga club firmly in control of his future.

The leading Premier League clubs are likely to have stepped up their interest after Gadou delivered a commendable performance in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyokeres put the hosts ahead inside the opening 10 minutes, but Gadou supplied the match’s defining moment in the 55th minute, earning Dortmund a valuable point.

The teenager surged forward from his own half, fended off two Arsenal challenges and played a decisive pass for Maximilian Beier to equalise.

In his 89 minutes in North London, Gadou also made four clearances and completed 19 of his 22 passes, drawing warm praise from head coach Niko Kovac.

Recent findings suggest that "We signed him because he is composed in possession and can contribute going forward," Kovac stated. "He can break the lines and regularly create chances for the strikers. He is also very quick with the ball. It was a truly impressive performance.”.

Bild via Sport Witness reports that Dortmund will not consider offers below four times the €20m (£16.8m)they paid Salzburg only months ago.

The club’s firm position is intended to discourage bids in January as Kovac's side aim to retain their key players for the second half of the 2026-27 campaign.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are not the only clubs linked with the Frenchman: former side Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are also reportedly interested.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in….

Recent findings suggest that I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

In a recent development, and to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s update was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

By the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, at the moment on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

It has been revealed that watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

As both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

Recent findings suggest that when Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Big Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

Closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a fresh long-term deal, while David Ornstein claims Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s upcoming contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive fresh contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be noted for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

Industry observers note that I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

It has been revealed that right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

New deals for all, Odegaard’s brilliance, assists galore

  • After Monday’s news that both Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice have agreed latest deals with the club, Tuesday brought the news that fellow 2023 signing David Raya was next in line, swiftly followed by reports that Riccardo Calafiori will also be handed a new deal, and Piero Hincapie will be getting improved terms, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, good morning! I’ve got to say, if I worked at Arsenal and I wasn’t getting a latest contract this international break, I think I’d be taking it pretty personally.

After Monday’s news that both Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice have agreed latest deals with the club, Tuesday brought the news that fellow 2023 signing David Raya was next in line, swiftly followed by reports that Riccardo Calafiori will also be handed a new deal, and Piero Hincapie will be getting improved terms, too.

Industry observers note that since the end of the 2024-25 season, there have already been newly introduced deals for Gabriel, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka, and, of course, Mikel Arteta. With the latest raft of agreements on top of those, that’s a lot of important people tied down for the next few years.

These deals will mean everyone other than Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Ben White, Mikel Merino, and Kepa is contracted to the club until at least 2029. That’s a nice feeling, isn’t it? There will be some decisions to be made over a couple of those players and whether it’s time to refresh, you’d imagine, but the bulk of the squad should be staying put and continuing to compete together – with a couple of additions supplementing them, of course – for the next couple of years at least.

Of those four (plus Kepa) mentioned above, you’d have to think Odegaard is the next priority when it comes to renewals, given his importance on and off the pitch and his current form.

I was in a bar here in Berlin catching up with a fellow Arsenal fan yesterday evening (hello, if you’re reading!) and they had Norway’s game in Denmark on. It’s fair to say the skipper continued his fine start to the season.

According to recent reports, after Norway went two down against the run of play, Odegaard sprung into action. No player had as many touches on the night, and he was involved in all three Norway goals.

Sources indicate that he stole the ball for the goal that made it 2-1, which, by the way, we should have a word for. We have the word equaliser for when it goes to 2-2, but we don’t have a word for the goal that shortens the lead. The Germans call it an Anschlusstor – literally a ‘connecting goal’, the goal that means the scores are now just one apart.

Anyway, Odegaard, pressing as he always does, stole the ball from goalkeeper Mads Hermansen, then selflessly left the tap-in for Erling Haaland. He then scored the equaliser, a goal reminiscent of his opening day strike against Coventry if we’re honest: he didn’t hit it well, he got a bit lucky. But: right place, right time and all that.

Recent findings suggest that and, finally, it was Odegaard’s ferociously whipped in free-kick that struck the hand of Joachim Andersen and allowed Haaland to convert from the penalty spot late into added time. If you’ve got a few minutes, you can see the highlights of his performance here – some of the touches are more than worth your time.

A good night’s work, especially after he was suffering with a stomach bug last week.

It wasn’t just the captain in action yesterday, either. Piero Hincapie played just over an hour for Ecuador overnight, there were assists for Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes as Brazil beat Singapore 7-0 earlier on in the day, and then an assist for Viktor Gyokeres too as Sweden drew with Poland.

That looks like something he’s clearly worked on – getting his body in the way of the defender and, rather than holding the ball up, looking to direct it towards an oncoming runner. His assist for Declan Rice in Munich obviously looked pretty similar, and it’s not something we saw too much of last season.

Industry observers note that in fact, I thought I’d have a quick look, and Gyokeres has 13 key passes (a pass that leads a shot from a team-mate) in the Premier League and Champions League this season. He’s delivering a key pass every 28.4 minutes. Last season he had a key pass every 104 minutes across those two competitions. It’s hard not to conclude that he’s been working on that side of his game, and these Giroud-esque back-to-goal touches for team-mates are more than welcome.

So, plenty of assists this break. Now we just need to harness that at Newcastle on Saturday and actually have someone to stick the ball in the back of the net at the end of those moves. Thankfully – knock on wood – it seems the players have made it through the break unscathed (there was also another behind-closed-doors appearance for William Saliba – a nod to Tom Canton for that story) and should be raring to go.

In a recent development, lastly, I want to point you towards Arseblog News, where Andrew A wrote something last night on the death of double-winner Peter Storey, one of just eight players to make over 500 appearances for the club. That first double is such an enormous part of our history wouldn’t have happened without Storey’s nerves of steel in the FA Cup semi-final.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that andrew M here after a couple of days ‘off’, but not the kind where you sit in a hammock and have delicious things brought to you. More the kind where you have three stab wounds in your abdomen and a chunk of your insides taken out. If at all possible, I seriously recommend the former to the latter. Anyway, I’m here right now with coffee and painkillers, which I guess is something akin to Arseblog heritage.

It has been revealed that the Interlull is over and that’s it now until March. It’s non-stop Arsenal all the way, and all the focus will be on us and what we can produce on the pitch. For those interested in what our players got up to during this break, and what they delivered for their respective nations, Andrew A has a handy round-up over on Arseblog News. Now it’s about keeping everyone as fit as possible, the manager using the squad in the smartest and most effective way he can, and for some of the players who are capable of producing more doing exactly that.

In a recent development, I was quite interested in Lewis’ quick look at Viktor Gyokeres and his key pass metrics from yesterday’s blog: He’s delivering a key pass every 28.4 minutes. Last season he had a key pass every 104 minutes across those two competitions [PL & CL].

I think sample size might be a factor here, because when you look at his xG per 90, it’s 0.05 per 90 in both Premier League and Champions League this season, versus .99 and .76 per 90 last season, but obviously he played more minutes last time out. After 14 appearances this season, he’s rustled up a total of 614 minutes; this time last season his first 14 appearances brought him a cumulative 1200+ minutes. The absence of Kai Havertz was a factor, obviously, but it was probably that early season load that contributed to the injury he picked up against Burnley after a solid first half performance.

In a recent development, the job for Mikel Arteta is to find a way to share those minutes effectively, to have both his strikers scoring and assisting, and to harness some of what Gyokeres has been able to produce for Sweden. It’s often mooted that as a team we need to play to his strengths more, but perhaps these key pass metrics show that the design is more about eliminating some of the weaknesses in his game to make him more effective in the final third for us. Let’s see how it goes.

In a recent development, meanwhile, the KMI (Key Match Incident) panel have ruled on the Kai Havertz penalty incident against Hull. They ruled 5-0 that the on-field decision was wrong and that VAR, manned that day by Michael Oliver, should have intervened:.

Although Havertz is clearly in an offside position, there is a clear and impactful holding action by Mendy before any potential offside offence by Havertz. Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded. The panel considered the VAR intervention was correct; however, the outcome after the on-field review was considered to be incorrect as a penalty should have been awarded.

Industry observers note that I get every day is a learning day for ‘ProRef’, the people whose job it is to know the rules of football but week after week seem to demonstrate in upcoming and inventive ways that they don’t. The question for us as fans is, what are we supposed to do with this? Are we supposed to feel better knowing that they’re owning up to mistakes? It feels a bit like getting run over when you have the green light at a pedestrian crossing, a nearby cop just lets the bloke go, but then later a judge indicates he should have been stopped and arrested.

According to recent reports, which is all well and good when you’re in a hospital bed in traction with a couple of broken legs and smashed pelvis (I say this only because I remember being in hospital with a bloke who fell under a bus and that’s what happened to him. He was fine though, his mates brought him in loads of joints which he used to share in the smoking room – this was 90s hospital). Which is to say, the damage has been done, the admission the bloke got it wrong in the first place doesn’t really make you feel any better.

Industry observers note that from our perspective at least, Martin Odegaard’s winner ensured that decision didn’t turn out to be one which went on to live in infamy – like not drawing the lines for that Brentford goal that time, but it’s still essentially useless. Not least because you just know this weekend or next weekend some other mad thing will happen and they’ll say ‘Oooops! Sorry about that LOL here’s Michael Owen and Howard Webb!’, and some team will lose points because they can’t properly apply the rules of the game to things that happen on the pitch.

Industry observers note that finally for today, we’re being linked with a January move for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. He’s certainly a fine player, but it doesn’t make a lot of sense to me given we already have the best midfield depth in the Premier League, and beyond. Where does he fit with Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Odegaard? Perhaps if, for example, Zubi went there’s a case to be made for a replacement, but as it is he’s struggling for minutes anyway, and you don’t pay that kind of money for someone to come in and be peripheral.

Recent findings suggest that like most of you, if there’s money to be spent in January, I’d much rather see it go on the forward line where I feel like there’s obvious room for improvement and to increase our depth. The left hand side is the obvious place, it’s hard not to worry about the right a little bit with Bukayo Saka’s injury, and the striker conversation is one which is never quite going to go away. So, on that basis, links to Scott don’t really add up for me. Unless Arteta fancies converting him to another left-back. Then it all clicks, but I think there’s one Bournemouth player we’d all rather see arrive.

According to recent reports, right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. In terms of a podcast, I’m not quite feeling up to it today, but what we’ll do is make our Patreon preview podcast free and available to everyone tomorrow afternoon. I should be less sore then, and I continue to be blown away by your many emails and messages. Thank you so much, they mean the world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25.

Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.

In a recent development, short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season. It was an underwhelming spell, during which the winger started only four times and was labelled a flop.

This season, Arsenal decided to send him out on loan again, this time to Borussia Dortmund.

Sources indicate that however, the England Under-21 international no longer really features in the aims of Niko Kovac. Although he was used on many occasions at the start of the season, Nwaneri has not been in Dortmund's starting line-up since 17 October, away to Union Berlin (0-0).

Since that game, he has made a string of appearances in the final minutes of matches and has been left on the bench for the significant games, against Bayern Munich (2-2) and Arsenal (1-1).

Sources indicate that as a result, the player, who belongs to Arsenal, has played only 29 minutes in the German club's last seven outings, which is insufficient game time. This situation could also benefit West Ham United.

According to FootballTransfers, West Ham are preparing a loan offer to bring Nwaneri to the club in January.

The London club, 13th in the Championship, are looking to strengthen their squad in an attempt to return to the Premier League. However, the deal is far from straightforward, as Arsenal will first have to recall their youngster from Dortmund.

The British outlet points out that Nwaneri's loan at Borussia Dortmund does not include an option or obligation to buy. Arsenal have a recall clause which gives them the possibility of bringing their youngster back in January.

However, the Bundesliga leaders paid a loan fee, reportedly between £3.4m and £4.3m (€4m-€5m), and are covering the player's wages. Therefore, if Arsenal activate the recall clause for Nwaneri, they would have to reimburse the loan fee to Borussia Dortmund.

It therefore remains to be seen whether Arsenal will be prepared to give up that compensation to allow their talented youngster to join an environment more conducive to his progress, and whether the London club will demand another paid loan this winter.

West Ham are, in any case, lurking and ready to position themselves for the deal.

  • Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.
