#153123. Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1066 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

As a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find upcoming forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

Countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," said Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

It has been revealed that she says it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it highlights it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She says it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott mentioned.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Sources indicate that since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national aims to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no upcoming commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Kumar indicates more countries could announce similar aims just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

Recent findings suggest that the nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

In a recent development, the roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

It has been revealed that kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

It has been revealed that global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald highlights that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing fresh reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One glitch Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar stated, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

Virgil van Dijk is now in the final year of his Liverpool contract.

The Dutchman has been one of the Reds' best players since he joined in 2017 and, without him, Liverpool wouldn't have won half as much as they have.

However, by the time the 2027-28 season kicks off, the Dutchman will be 36 years old and will be entering the twilight stages of his career.

Indeed, he did hit his prime a bit later than most players so he could continue playing at the top level for a while.

But, because the Reds can't be sure of this, they're holding back on offering the Dutchman a latest deal for now.

Many different centre-backs have been linked with Liverpool as their next Virgil van Dijk but, there's one stand-out candidate who the Reds have just been handed a massive boost to sign.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool a clear run at Nico Schlotterbeck.

Liverpool, Barcelona and Manchester United have all been fairly intertwined with transfer links recently.

All three teams seem to want the same players in the same positions and, while one of them are bound to end up signing them, they'll drive the price up for each other which doesn't really make much sense.

However, since most of the world's biggest clubs all want to sign the best players, these links are rarely ever going to die down but, fortunately for Liverpool, Barcelona seem to have turned their attention away from Nico Schlotterbeck.

That is, if this latest upgrade from BBC Sport is to be believed.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

In a recent development, "At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.".

Nico Schlotterbeck is who Liverpool need to replace Virgil van Dijk.

One of the best things about Schlotterbeck is the fact that he's left-footed.

The German can also be used as a centre-back or a left-back if needed.

His entire career has been spent in Germany but, most of his experience of competitions such as the Champions League have come with Borussia Dortmund.

Last summer, he signed a newly introduced contract with the German outfit but, there is a release clause in his contract for certain clubs across the globe, including Liverpool.

The exact price of this clause is unknown but, the fact that Liverpool are one of them means that he clearly wants to make the move.

He's also only 26 years old so, even though he has plenty of experience under his belt, there's still room for him to grow.

Here's hoping that Liverpool get this deal over the line, especially now that Barcelona seem to be turning their attention away from him.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 10:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 04:18 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • The voice of the late BBC commentator John Motson will be featured on the EA Sports FC 27 video game through 'a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation'.
  • Motson, who died at the age of 77 in 2023, had served as the lead commentator on BBC's football coverage for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 10:33 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 04:18 EST, 26 November 2026.

The voice of the late BBC commentator John Motson will be featured on the EA Sports FC 27 video game through 'a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation'.

Motson, who died at the age of 77 in 2023, had served as the lead commentator on BBC's football coverage for decades.

The legendary commentator had also lent his voice to Electronic Arts's FIFA series of games in the 1990s and 2000s.

EA has revealed that it has worked with the blessing and in partnership with Motson's family to have him feature as an optional commentary selection in an patch of the latest edition of their EA Sports FC game.

The publisher stated its development studio 'has put Motson back into the commentary box with the aid of new AI-tools, bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself.'.

EA stated its team worked with 'extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game's greatest voices'.

The late BBC commentator John Motson will feature on the EA Sports FC 27 video game, through recordings and AI recreation.

Motson's family gave permission for the late commentator, who died in 2023, to feature in the game.

'My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,' said Fred Motson, son of John Motson.

'His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole new set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.'.

Motson's son also told the BBC his father would have 'absolutely' wanted to be involved in the game after his death.

The BBC reported that Motson's family were paid for the rights to use his likeness and to recreate his voice in the game.

EA added that AI had been the 'only way' for Motson's voice to feature, as there were no recordings of him talking about modern players.

While Motson's family gave EA's project their blessing, the use of AI to recreate voices has become an increasingly controversial topic.

In August, a group of 80 performers backed the Save Our Voices Now campaign, which is seeking to secure legal protection against technology which can clone a person's voice and make it say anything its operator chooses.

The campaign was founded by actor and voice artist Peter Caulfield and has been backed by stars including Hugh Bonneville, Nicola Coughlan and Matt Lucas.

Campaigners want Britain to follow the example set by Denmark, which has moved to give its citizens full legal control over AI-generated imitations of their face, body and voice.

The protections allow people to demand that any unauthorised content is removed and seek compensation for its misuse.

Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (864 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.
  • "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.
  • But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has become the latest prominent football figure to call for change at the top of FIFA.

"Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job," he remarked on Sunday.

But with time running out before the November 18 deadline for new candidates for the presidency of world football's governing body, Infantino is looking overwhelmingly likely to win another term.

"There are people who truly care about the future of football, people who aren't driven by financial interests," Klopp noted ahead of Germany's Nations League match against the Netherlands on Monday.

"If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.".

If that person is waiting in the wings, they're leaving it late to step on the stage. Despite a raft of federations and continental confederations, including Germany, UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and AFC (Asia), calling for Infantino's head in the wake of his plan to sell off part of the World Cup earlier this year, the incumbent appears to have stopped the bleeding.

That plan, which involved forming a subsidiary arm of FIFA called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) in order to sell off part of its commercial operations to investors including Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner — was widely panned before being abandoned.

It followed on from widespread criticism of Infantino's awarding of a new FIFA Peace Prize to Trump, the overturning of a red card for US national team player Folarin Balogun, and with Trump's involvement, at the World Cup and a host of other controversies.

Since then, though, many public critics have backtracked amid FIFA promising to release an extra $2.7bn (€2.45bn) from its reserves over the next four years to the federations, increasing their total investment to $6.35bn.

Perhaps the most significant of these u-turns came from the AFC, who went from saying Infantino had committed a "fundamental breach of trust" in August, to offering the Swiss its "full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a upcoming mandate as the FIFA president" in October.

Industry observers note that those words were spoken by AFC President, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, who ran against Infantino when he first won the top job at FIFA in 2016. He will not run again and remarked that "my feeling is, I'm sure, the feeling of most of my members," in regard to Infantino.

In a recent development, proof that the sentiment is not universal comes in the shape of Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA). Tashima is one of only two people to confirm they will oppose Infantino in the March 2027 presidential elections.

The 68-year-old is a well respected figure in Asian football politics and will have no problem meeting the threshold of support from five of FIFA's 211 federations. This is not like the other candidate, former Swiss international player Ramon Vega, who is an enormous outsider. Tashima appears to be running on the basis that he will be able to chart a calmer path at FIFA.

Recent findings suggest that "I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association," Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. "It's not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.".

Recent findings suggest that but the numbers are against him. Though support from within the confederations may not be total, the backing of AFC and the African confederation (CAF) is a huge boost for Infantino, with those two alone making up 101 votes, almost enough for a majority.

It has been revealed that in fact, the only real concern remaining for Infantino remains UEFA. The European federation, headed by Aleksander Ceferin, is a major revenue source for FIFA but the two organizations are at loggerheads. As well as a war of words, UEFA are seeking to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against Infantino in regards to FFE. FIFA have called this a "smear campaign" and a "fishing expedition".

But, so far, UEFA has not put up a candidate. Former Arsenal coach turned FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger was thought to be a contender but has now ruled himself out. Wenger's compatriot, Philippe Diallo, has since emerged as another option, with The Guardian reporting on Monday that the French Football Federation president could be confirmed on Tuesday.

While Europe is football's powerbase, particularly from a club perspective, UEFA will need Diallo, or any candidate they can convince to run, to win votes from outside its 55 nations to have any chance of success, particularly with Tashima likely to split any challenge. Even if a candidate appears before the November 18 deadline, Klopp's hope for change appears to be a long shot.

The Catalan giants have won four of their last five matches against Deportivo, including a famous 8-0 success in the corresponding game during the 2015-16 campaign.

These two teams have locked horns on 105 previous occasions throughout history, and it is Barcelona that leads the overall head-to-head record 63 wins to Deportivo's 22, while 20 of their encounters have finished all square.

Barcelona are three points ahead of second-placed Real Madrid and five clear of third-placed Atletico Madrid, and they posted a 3-2 success over Villarreal in their last league fixture.

The Blaugrana have the best home record in La Liga this season, picking up 18 points from seven matches, while they are comfortably the highest goalscorers in Spain's top flight during the 2026-27 campaign, finding the back of the net on 51 occasions.

COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).
  • The goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text.
  • Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

The goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The newly introduced negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," noted Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

According to recent reports, "For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," said Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but mentioned it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she said in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

"Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," stated Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," remarked Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

It has been revealed that at 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

In a recent development, "The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," noted Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

It has been revealed that "The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have mentioned to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text showed a level of "seriousness" on important issues like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

"The question is whether the level of ambition on those concerns is carried through into the final outcome here," stated Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

Update, November 17, 2026: This article has been updated with additional reactions to the draft text.

It has been revealed that liverpool's big problem with signing a midfielder has been Chelsea. The Blues also need a high-profile midfielder, having sold Enzo Fernandez at the transfer deadline without a replacement.

In a recent development, they did try to sign one, of course. Lamine Camara was a serious option and they did bid. AS Monaco ended the deal right at the death, however, as they felt a bigger one could be had in 2027 - Liverpool were supposedly the reason why, essentially.

Alex Scott is another heavily linked with Liverpool, especially as his former coach, Iraola, is in charge at Anfield. But Chelsea were supposed to be ahead in that race, going all-out for the Bournemouth star.

According to recent reports, but David Ornstein reports that Chelsea aren't actually going for a midfielder right now, in what's a massive surprise to everyone. He told USA Sports that he's not aware of any January ideas from the club. Instead, it appears they're going to wait for the summer.

That leaves the door wide open for Liverpool, who could conceivably make a move for an elite midfielder before Chelsea even get to the table. Their biggest rival for competition isn't putting up a fight - and that's a huge advantage in any talks.

It stops the price rising too high, it stops players' heads getting turned, and it also takes away an immediate time pressure to strike a deal. Though, there is still the time pressure of getting it done in January.

But there's no question about it: Chelsea's stance is an advantage for Liverpool if the Reds are still happy to sign a midfield player.

#153108. Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease

Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 100 min read (20084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~100 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2.
  • Sources indicate that common diseases are driven by a multitude of factors and remain difficult to treat given the lack of a unified disease mechanism4.
  • Although population-scale GWAS offer great opportunity for target discovery, most identified variants lie within non-coding regions of the genome, making it difficult to dissect the causal cell types and molecular pathways13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956-mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

Sources indicate that common diseases are driven by a multitude of factors and remain difficult to treat given the lack of a unified disease mechanism4. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is among the most prevalent common chronic diseases, and numerous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have now identified hundreds of variants linked to CAD risk. Although these results may potentially pave the way for fresh therapeutic target discovery1,2,5,6, much of the translation from GWAS to therapeutic targets for CAD has been restricted to lipid-lowering drugs7,8. Large-scale clinical studies have demonstrated a persistent residual risk of CAD independent of lipid levels9,10, but we lack drugs that directly target disease pathways in the vessel wall due to an incomplete understanding of causal disease mechanisms. Leveraging human genetics to uncover new lipid-independent biological mechanisms and drug targets in CAD represents a tremendous unmet need and would be a principal milestone in translating population-scale GWAS findings to therapies for patients11,12.

Although population-scale GWAS offer great opportunity for target discovery, most identified variants lie within non-coding regions of the genome, making it difficult to dissect the causal cell types and molecular pathways13. The advent of single-cell sequencing technologies now allows for the profiling of human tissues in health and disease at unprecedented granularity14. Previous studies have used traditional single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) for detailed characterization of cell states in human tissue that drive disease15,16,17,18; however, these studies do not profile the non-coding genome, making it challenging to link GWAS variants to observed molecular changes. More recently, single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) with sequencing (snATAC–seq) in human coronary arteries was conducted to link CAD GWAS variants to regulatory elements19. Although this represented an notable advance in the field, the lack of complementary transcriptomic profiling rendered it challenging to nominate causal genes in vascular cell types. Furthermore, isolated snATAC–seq precludes the discovery of distal gene regulation as a driver of disease20, and there are currently no studies that profile the three-dimensional (3D) chromatin architecture in human coronary arteries to enable the investigation of these distal regulatory connections.

Herein we performed simultaneous multi-omic profiling of the transcriptome and epigenome in nuclei from 44 human coronary arteries to build a multi-omic enhancer–gene map of CAD. Collectively, these analyses identified CAD-associated regulatory variants and enhancer–gene links in smooth muscle cells (SMCs), motivating focused analysis of SMC state-dependent gene regulation. To expand insight into gene regulation across functionally heterogeneous SMC cell states, we used dynamic chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTL) modelling to uncover cell-state-dependent pathogenicity of disease variants. To dissect the role of disease-associated variants in regulating larger scale gene networks, we performed genome-wide Hi-C in 15 human coronary arteries to link variants to distal genes and validated our findings using cell-specific high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) with chromatin immunoprecipitation (Hi-ChIP–seq) and in vitro CRISPRi. Finally, we performed Perturb–seq in human coronary artery SMCs (HCASMCs) to characterize functional mechanisms of repressing disease-associated enhancers and genes. Collectively, we provide a multi-omic map of human CAD by integrating transcriptomic, epigenetic and chromatin architecture to link disease-associated genetic variants with candidate disease-relevant cell types and target genes.

We performed single-nucleus Multi-ome (RNA+ATAC) sequencing in 44 human coronary arteries from non-failing donors and patients with chronic heart failure isolated at the time of heart transplantation (Fig. 1a, Supplementary Fig. 1a and Supplementary Table 1). After quality control, we recovered 126,804 nuclei from 11 distinct cell types (Fig. 1b,c and Supplementary Fig. 1b–d). Using differential expression of canonical genes, we identified clusters corresponding to all main vascular cell types, including coronary artery SMCs (MYH11, ACTA2, ITGA8), endothelial cells (VWF, LDB2, PECAM1), fibroblasts (LAMA2, DCN, FBLN1) and myeloid cells (F13A1, CD163, MRC1) (Fig. 1b, Extended Data Fig. 1a–c and Supplementary Table 2). We used MACS2 to identify areas of open chromatin (‘peaks’) from the ATAC–seq data (Fig. 1e) and identified 143,743 cell-type-specific differentially accessible peaks (Extended Data Fig. 1d,e). Generally, cell-type clustering was concordant between the RNA and ATAC data. However, gene-expression data enabled the annotation of rarer cell types that were not captured by ATAC-based clustering alone (Supplementary Fig. 1e–g). Using differentially accessible peaks across cells, we also discovered cell-type-specific enrichment of transcriptional motifs such as SpiB and PU.1 in myeloid cells, MEF2B/C/D in SMCs and CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein in adipocytes (Supplementary Fig. 1h). We linked peaks to genes using a new supervised single-cell model called single-cell enhancer-to-gene (E2G) (scE2G)21 (Fig. 1d, Extended Data Fig. 2a–g and Supplementary Tables 3–14; Methods). We found that the non-immune cells had the greatest number of shared enhancers relative to myeloid cells (Fig. 1d) and that all cell types had a similar number of E2G links (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Table 3).

NK, natural killer. d, Number of shared enhancers heatmap (right) from scE2G map (left); defined as the number of enhancers where more than 50% of the peak width overlaps with other cell type-specific peaks. e, Number of scE2G links in the main cell types. f, Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) for cardiometabolic traits by cell type; dotted line, multiple-testing-adjusted P value threshold. P values were calculated using one-sided stratified LDSC, with Bonferroni correction for six conditions (P < 8.33 × 10−3). Sources indicate that notably, we found that cardiometabolic disease variants for CAD, systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) were enriched in differentially accessible marker peaks specific to SMCs and endothelial cells (Fig. 1f). As a predominantly non-vascular trait, diabetes did not demonstrate enrichment of disease-associated variants (Fig. 1f).

It has been revealed that to boost our power for single-cell caQTL (sc-caQTL) discovery, we integrated our Multi-ome ATAC–seq data with available snATAC–seq data from human coronary arteries19 to create a meta-map of 88 samples and 245,562 nuclei across four ancestry groups (Extended Data Fig. 3a–f). We then used RASQUAL to identify pseudobulk caQTLs in four principal vascular cell types (SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts) (Fig. 2a). At the 10% false discovery rate (FDR) threshold, we found 11,269 significant caQTL associations in SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells and fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 3g–i, Supplementary Fig. 2a–d and Supplementary Tables 15–26). Power, sensitivity, subsampling and runtime analyses are shown in Supplementary Figs. 2 and 3 and described in Supplementary Methods.

The P value was calculated using a two-sided t-test of the GTEx eQTL linear regression coefficient against zero. f, PRINT and seq2PRINT transcription factor binding prediction pipeline (left). rs658956 overlaps region with high transcription factor binding probability from seq2PRINT model (top) and multiscale footprinting associates rs658956 with a transcription factor-specific footprint (bottom). g, Motif analysis finds rs658956 overlaps canonical AP-1 transcription factor (JUN, FOS) motifs. Ref, reference alelle; Alt, alternate allele. h, EMSA demonstrates a binding shift in the reference allele sequence (containing G) that was not present in the alternative allele sequence (containing T) when these allelic sequences were exposed to nuclear lysate from SMCs (n = 3 replicates, representative experiment shown). i, Dynamic caQTL modelling and discovery strategy (cell-state-dependent). j, rs658956 caQTL dynamic effect size. Net effect size depicted here represents the sum of \({\beta }_{g}\) and \({\beta }_{{\rm{F}}{\rm{M}}{\rm{C}}{\rm{x}}{\rm{G}}}\) in our generalized linear mixed model across cells. k, rs658956 genotype association with normalized chromatin accessibility across FMC tertiles. Negative slope of association increases as FMC score increases; n = 268 (e) and n = 79 (k) biologically independent samples were used. In a recent development, we further characterized caQTL variants to assess their regulatory potential. Lead caQTL variants were enriched strongly near the peaks they were predicted to regulate, consistent with a cis-regulatory mechanism (Extended Data Fig. 3j). We next overlapped our pseudobulk caQTLs and GTEx bulk arterial tissue eQTLs by cell type and found several hundred shared QTL variants in SMCs, endothelial cells, myeloid cells and fibroblasts (Extended Data Fig. 3i). Furthermore, we found a strong correlation in effect size between our SMC caQTLs and bulk coronary artery eQTLs from GTEx (Extended Data Fig. 3k). Finally, in SMCs we trained a convolutional neural net model (seq2PRINT22) that incorporates chromatin accessibility and ATAC footprinting to predict transcription factor binding probability at a base-pair resolution. We found that caQTL variants within accessible peaks had significantly higher predicted transcription factor binding probabilities compared with all other non-caQTL SNP sites within accessible peaks (P = 8.2 × 10−40, Wilcoxon rank sum) (Extended Data Fig. 3l).

It has been revealed that to identify disease-associated caQTLs, we overlapped sc-caQTLs for each cell type with CAD GWAS variants (defined as lead variants associated with CAD at 1% FDR1 and variants in linkage disequilibrium with these at R2 ≥ 0.8 in the European population from 1000 Genomes Project; Supplementary Table 27), which yielded numerous disease-relevant cell-type-specific caQTLs (Extended Data Fig. 3m). For example, we found that rs7182567 was an SMC-specific caQTL that was also a GWAS variant (P = 5.4 × 10−26) and a bulk GTEx eQTL for ADAMTS7 in tibial artery (Extended Data Fig. 4a). Similarly, we found that rs8017642 is an endothelial cell-specific caQTL in the NEK9 locus (Extended Data Fig. 4b), whereas rs2337154 and rs1443120 are fibroblast- and myeloid-specific caQTLs, respectively (Extended Data Fig. 4c,d).

Recent findings suggest that next, we leveraged the paired RNA data to sub-cluster SMCs into transcriptionally distinct cell states, forming a continuum from ‘healthy’ contractile SMC states (SMC1–3) to de-differentiated ‘disease-associated’ SMC states including fibromyocytes (FMCs) and chondromyocytes (CMCs) (Extended Data Fig. 4e). Notably, we found that ADAMTS7 was expressed most highly in FMCs (Extended Data Fig. 4e), indicating a role in disease regulation. To identify functionally distinct endothelial cell states, we mapped our data to a high-resolution scRNA-seq atherosclerosis atlas23 and identified four transcriptionally distinct endothelial subsets (Extended Data Fig. 4f). Notably, NEK9 was expressed in endothelial cells enriched with endothelium-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) genes such as COL1A1 and FN1 (refs. 24,25) (Extended Data Fig. 4f,g). Pathway enrichment in the EMT population indicated increased EMT and stress-response signals (Extended Data Fig. 4h). Next, we created a gene set score comprised of 41 endothelial cell-specific genes thought to be associated causally with CAD26 that showed maximal enrichment in intimal endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 4i). Similarly, we created a gene signature of a gene programme26 identified previously as driving CAD pathogenesis in endothelial cells (Programme 8) and found an enrichment of this programme in angiogenic and/or vasa vasorum endothelial cells (Extended Data Fig. 4j).

The CAD disease-associated variant rs658956 illustrates how a cell-type-specific caQTL can impart functional transcriptional changes. The variant is an SMC-specific and fibroblast-specific caQTL and regulates a putative enhancer element (chr. 1: 59169569–59170069), which is linked to the gene FGGY-DT in an SMC-specific manner by scE2G (Fig. 2c,d). Consistently, we found that rs658956 is also a coronary artery eQTL for FGGY-DT expression (P = 3.4 × 10−12) wherein the alternative allele (T) is associated with decreased expression relative to the reference allele (G) (Fig. 2e) and is also predicted to overlie a high probability transcription factor binding site (Fig. 2f). Motif-based transcription factor binding site analysis found that rs658956 is predicted to disrupt a core AP-1 (JUN/FOS) transcription factor binding motif (5′-TGAGTCA-3′) (Fig. 2g). Electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) demonstrated a binding shift in the reference allele sequence (containing G) that was not present in the alternative allele sequence (containing T) when these alleles were exposed to nuclear lysate from SMCs (Fig. 2h). Antibody supershift EMSA confirmed that the shifted AP-1 complex band consists of JUN and FOS transcription factors (Extended Data Fig. 4k). Together, these results suggest that the disease-associated variant rs658956 impacts transcription factor binding, thereby decreasing the chromatin accessibility of the enhancer and subsequently reducing FGGY-DT expression in a SMC-specific manner.

Recent findings suggest that in atherosclerosis, SMCs undergo a well-characterized phenotypic switch from a contractile state to a fibroblast-like FMC phenotype16, driven by disease-associated transcriptional programmes. To characterize this transition, individual nuclei were assigned an FMC score based on FMC state marker genes for downstream modelling (Fig. 2i and Extended Data Fig. 5a–d). Notably, this FMC gene score is dynamic with disease across species, disease burden, pseudotime trajectory, in vitro HCASMC stress and transcriptional regulation (Extended Data Fig. 5e–k). To identify state-dependent caQTL effects, we used a Poisson mixed-effects (PME) single-cell model (Extended Data Fig. 6a–c; Methods). Applying this PME model to the lead variants of SMC-specific pseudobulk caQTLs, we identified 712 caQTLs whose effects were dynamic with respect to the FMC score (FDR ≤ 5%) (Supplementary Tables 29 and 30). Notably, eight of these dynamic caQTLs were also disease-associated variants. For example, rs658956 exhibited a significant interaction with FMC score (FDR-adjusted likelihood ratio test (LRT) P value = 2.36 × 10−4) (Fig. 2j,k). A negative interaction term indicates that, as the FMC score increased, the negative association between rs658956 and local chromatin accessibility was amplified (Fig. 2j,k). Using the scE2G map to link dynamic caQTL-related enhancer elements (caPeaks) to target genes, we found that extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling was the most enriched pathway among linked genes (Extended Data Fig. 6d,e and Supplementary Table 31). Notably, several of these genes linked to dynamic caPeaks were enriched in FMCs (Extended Data Fig. 6f and Supplementary Table 32). Similar state-dependent effects were observed at other CAD loci such as dynamic caQTL variant rs11838776 in the COL4A1 locus, suggesting that COL4A1 may play a role during transition toward an FMC state (Extended Data Fig. 6g–k). Collectively, these dynamic analyses demonstrate that disease-associated variants can exert cell-state-dependent regulatory effects on chromatin accessibility.

In a recent development, to map CAD disease-associated variants to cell types and genes in an unbiased fashion, we built a disease-relevant single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map (scV2E2G) integrating cell-type-specific regulatory elements, CAD GWAS variants, scE2G links and caQTLs21,27 (Fig. 3a; Methods).

Overlapping scE2G with sc-caQTLs provides a high-fidelity set of predicted variants that may be driving disease by directly regulating intermediate molecular traits in a cell-type-specific manner.

Focusing on the 325 genes linked to SMC enhancers harbouring CAD GWAS variants, we performed several enrichment analyses. These analyses found that these linked genes were over-represented in nearest lead genes from CAD and myocardial infarction GWAS, identified GATA2 as the most enriched transcription factor and highlighted collagen and ECM remodelling as key biological processes (Extended Data Fig. 7a and Supplementary Tables 37–39). Correlation analysis between gene expression and FMC score identified FN1, COL4A1, COL4A2, MFGE8 and MYO9B—all known CAD-associated genes implicated in ECM remodelling—among the most highly correlated transcripts (Extended Data Fig. 7b and Supplementary Table 40). Notably, the enhancer harbouring variant rs7246865 emerged as potentially vital in disease, acting as both a cell-state dynamic caPeak and pseudobulk caPeak in SMCs with a high-confidence scE2G link (Fig. 3b). We confirmed this predicted link experimentally using CRISPRi in HCASMCs. Repressing the rs7246865-containing enhancer significantly reduced MYO9B expression relative to a non-targeting control (Fig. 3c), consistent with previous functional validation at this locus1. Furthermore, CRISPRi validated scE2G predictions in SMCs for three additional loci near genes LOXL1, NAV1 and PALLD; enhancer repression altered gene expression significantly at each of these loci relative to non-targeting controls (Extended Data Fig. 7c–e).

According to recent reports, to further validate scE2G links, we performed arrayed CRISPRi Perturb–seq in HCASMCs, delivering individual sgRNAs to target either the transcription start site (TSS) or the nominated enhancer at eight CAD GWAS loci (Fig. 3d, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 41). Alongside transcriptional profiling, we measured SMC proliferation by live-cell imaging, revealing that several perturbations (including ADAMTS7, CFDP1 and COL4A1) and significantly reduced proliferation rate, with enhancer knockdowns generally phenocopying their cognate TSS perturbations (Fig. 3e, Extended Data Fig. 8a and Supplementary Table 42). Following quality control, we retained 76,179 cells and confirmed robust, perturbation-specific transcriptional responses, with selective target-gene knockdown, stronger effects for TSS than enhancer perturbations and separation from non-targeting controls (Extended Data Fig. 8b–j).

According to recent reports, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed locus-specific pathway enrichments: BMP1 and ADAMTS7 knockdowns strongly enriched MYC and E2F target-gene sets, whereas CFDP1 and COL4A1 knockdowns suppressed interferon response pathways, indicating distinct downstream transcriptional consequences across CAD loci (Extended Data Fig. 9a). Consensus non-negative matrix factorization identified six biologically interpretable programmes: inflammation, ECM remodelling, vascular remodelling, interferon response and two proliferative programmes corresponding to S and M phase (Extended Data Fig. 9b,c and Supplementary Tables 43 and 44). Notably, the ECM remodelling programme showed the strongest positive correlation with the FMC module score, with enhancer knockdowns of CFDP1, MYO9B and BMP1 exhibiting the highest mean FMC scores (Extended Data Fig. 9d–h). Programme-level analysis further revealed that COL4A1 and its enhancer were the strongest drivers of the inflammation programme, whereas the MRAS and CFDP1 enhancer perturbations modulated both inflammation and ECM remodelling (Fig. 3f).

Finally, robust rank aggregation (RRA) across pseudobulk DESeq2 profiles revealed a convergent gene programme dominated by downregulation of several collagen genes (COL3A1, COL4A1, COL5A1, COL6A1–A3) and TIMP2, alongside the upregulation of metabolic and stress-response genes (Fig. 3g, Extended Data Fig. 9i and Supplementary Table 45). Pathway enrichment of this convergent programme identified EMT, tumour necrosis factor signalling through nuclear factor κB, and mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 signalling as the top enriched terms (Fig. 3h). Collectively, these findings implicate a shared regulatory framework that governs SMC phenotypic states across independent, disease-associated loci.

According to recent reports, to investigate how disease-associated variants may influence broader gene networks through chromatin looping, we performed genome-wide Hi-C in 15 human coronary arteries to construct large-scale chromatin networks (Fig. 4a, Extended Data Fig. 10a–f and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). To further complement Hi-C in bulk tissue, we performed H3K27Ac Hi-ChIP–seq in cultured human coronary artery smooth muscle cells and endothelial cells. Comparing the number of enhancer–gene connection overlap by method, we found that scE2GMulti-ome and Hi-ChIP yielded the highest number of enhancer–gene connections, with a smaller fraction from bulk coronary tissue Hi-C (Supplementary Fig. 7). We then identified groups of genomic loci that interact preferentially with one another in specific chromatin networks termed ‘mosaics’ (Fig. 4a; Methods). We identified 5,130 mosaics containing 11,494 protein-coding genes. Notably, mosaics harbouring a disease-associated variant exhibited significantly higher structural complexity, containing an average of 25 loops compared with 14 loops in non-disease-associated mosaics (P = 1.7 × 10−17) (Fig. 4b). This approach provides a framework for mapping disease-associated variants to a catalogue of genes regulated distally through interconnected chromatin networks (Supplementary Tables 46–49).

a, Study design and computational framework with inherent normalization for looping and TAD analysis from tissue Hi-C data. b, Number of loops in mosaics with and without a CAD variant demonstrates significantly greater number of Hi-C loops in mosaics that contain at least one CAD variant. Data represent medians ± interquartile range. c, Mosaic prioritization by number of genes and SMC enhancers containing a CAD variant. d, Boundary loop in mosaic-1664 originating at rs4887091; heatmaps: left, participant homozygous for the reference allele T|T; right, participant homozygous for the alternate allele C|C. The enlarged area shows loop contact coloured by inherent score. e, Inherent score of the boundary loop from d in all samples grouped by genotypes at rs4887091, where each bar represents a single person. f, Allele-specific loops from phased genotype framework (left) and boundary loop inherent score resolved from phased genotypes showing increased looping strength in the reference allele (C) at rs4887091. Data represent means ± s.e.m. g, CTCF ChIP–seq in HCASMCs overlaid with SMC snATAC–seq and scE2G at the rs4887091 locus. h, rs4887091 ref (T) to alt is predicted to create a CTCF binding site. i, Haplotype-resolved CTCF ChIP–seq in HCASMCs from different cells that are homozygous (T|T), heterozygous (T|C) and homozygous (C|C) showing a dosage-dependent binding by genotype at rs4887091; n = 3 biologically independent samples were used. Data represent means ± s.e.m. In b and f, n = 15 biologically independent samples were used to construct the mosaics and derive allele-specific loops; data represent means ± s.e.m.; P values were calculated using the Mann–Whitney U test.

Next, we performed CTCF ChIP–seq in HCASMC to prioritize disease-associated SMC enhancers that are bound by CTCF. Of all CAD disease-associated variants, 498 overlapped CTCF peaks, including 200 within accessible chromatin regions. CAD-associated variants were enriched significantly at CTCF-bound regions above permutation-based expectation (1.25-fold, P = 0.02; Extended Data Fig. 10g).

In a recent development, among the top-ranking regulatory mosaics, we identified mosaic-1664, which contains the CAD-associated variant rs4887091 located within an SMC enhancer (Fig. 4c). In this mosaic, we found an 800-kb boundary loop exhibiting a strong rs4887091 genotype-dependent increase in contact strength for the alternate allele (C) relative to the reference allele (T) (Fig. 4d). Specifically, the loop strength increased in a dose-dependent manner when quantified across all samples, where there was minimal contact strength in homozygotes (T|T), moderate strength in heterozygotes (T|C, C|T) and highest strength in homozygotes (C|C) (Fig. 4e). Phased genotypes confirmed increased looping strength on the C allele (P = 3.1 × 10−3) (Fig. 4f).

It has been revealed that to characterize the regulatory architecture of rs4887091 within mosaic-1664, we identified all genes linked to the SMC enhancer containing rs4887091: Hi-C identified a boundary loop containing ADAMTS7, MORF4L1, CHRNA3, IDH3A, ACSBG1, CIB2, SH2D7 and TBC1D2 promoters (Fig. 4d), whereas scE2G identified ADAMTS7 (the nearest gene) (Fig. 4g). Consistent with ADAMTS7 being a functional target of this regulatory element, CRISPRi Perturb–seq targeting the rs4887091-containing enhancer reduced ADAMTS7 expression in HCASMCs (Extended Data Fig. 8f). CTCF ChIP–seq in HCASMCs demonstrated that rs4887091 overlaps a CTCF binding site (Fig. 4g). Furthermore, motif-based transcription factor binding site analysis found that rs4887091, which changes the reference (T) to alternate (C) allele, is predicted to create a core CTCF binding motif (Fig. 4h). Consistent with this prediction, haplotype-resolved CTCF ChIP–seq demonstrated allelic dosage-dependent increases in CTCF occupancy on the C allele (P = 0.0003) (Fig. 4i). Validation at control loci and orthogonal TaqMan genotyping confirmed the accuracy of the haplotype-resolved CTCF occupancy measurements (Extended Data Fig. 10h–j). Together, these data support a model in which rs4887091 creates an allele-specific CTCF binding site associated with increased local chromatin loop strength, although the effect of this loop alteration on gene expression remains to be established.

Although our scE2G predictions are limited to enhancer–gene interactions within a cis-window, leveraging Hi-C data can link CAD GWAS variants to distal genes. For the loops present in all 15 samples, we catalogued genes linked to a CAD GWAS variant through direct chromatin contact between putative enhancers and promoters and identified 11 such genes: ANTXR1, ARMC12, CNNM2, FKBP5, CAPG, SH2D6, AMOTL2, NUAK2, RGS1, PLCL1 and FOXC2 (Fig. 5a). Among these, ANTXR1, CAPG, SH2D6, AMOTL2, NUAK2 and RGS1 are not the nearest genes. As an example, the CAD-associated variant rs9876658 was linked to AMOTL2 through a direct Hi-C contact. rs9876658 falls within a snATAC–seq peak in SMCs, endothelial cells and fibroblasts (but not myeloid cells) highlighting stroma-specific regulation (Fig. 5b). H3K27ac ChIP–seq showed that rs9876658 overlapped a H3K27ac peak in SMCs but not in endothelial cells (Fig. 5b). Hi-ChIP–seq further identified a direct loop between the rs9876658-containing enhancer and the AMOTL2 promoter in SMCs but not in endothelial cells (Fig. 5b). Collectively, these analyses predict that the enhancer containing rs9876658 functionally regulates expression of AMOTL2 in SMCs but not in endothelial cells.
